title: BigQuery MCP Server: What It Is & How To Set It Up In 2026
summary: BigQuery MCP server setup in 2026: Google's managed endpoint vs MCP Toolbox, a least-privilege service account, cost caps, and what BigQuery's own AI adds.
body_markdown:
A BigQuery MCP server gives an AI client such as Claude, Cursor or Gemini CLI tools to read your BigQuery schemas and run SQL. Google offers two: the **managed BigQuery MCP server** , a remote endpoint with nothing to install, and the open-source **MCP Toolbox for Databases** , which you run yourself. Neither is read-only out of the box: the managed server's` execute_sql` tool can run DML and DDL, and the toolbox runs any statement unless you block writes. The safeguards that hold are a least-privilege identity for the server to run as and a cap on the bytes its queries may bill.


Both servers are free; the queries they run are billed like any other. BigQuery also has AI of its own (Gemini in BigQuery, data canvas and Conversational Analytics agents), covered after the setup. Everything below is as of October 2026, with Google's sources linked.


## The two BigQuery MCP servers at a glance


****


**Google-managed BigQuery MCP server**


**MCP Toolbox for Databases**


Where it runs


Google's endpoint,` https://bigquery.googleapis.com/mcp` ; nothing to install


Your machine or server, started with` npx`


Sign-in


Google Cloud IAM, through OAuth


Application Default Credentials, an impersonated service account, or each user's OAuth token


SQL tools


` execute_sql_readonly` (` SELECT` only) and` execute_sql` , which also runs DML and DDL


` execute_sql` , dataset and table metadata, forecasting, contribution analysis


Read-only control


The roles of the identity it runs as


` BIGQUERY_READONLY=true` , a dataset allowlist, and the identity's roles


Cost


Free; queries billed as usual


Free software; queries billed; a per-query bytes cap


## Option 1: Google's managed BigQuery MCP server


Google[announced official MCP support on December 10, 2025](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/announcing-official-mcp-support-for-google-services) : the BigQuery MCP server lets agents "natively interpret schemas and execute queries against enterprise data without the security risks or latency of moving data into context windows." By[April 29, 2026](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/google-managed-mcp-servers-are-available-for-everyone) , Google said more than 50 Google-managed MCP servers were generally available or in preview, and that "every Google Cloud service is now MCP-enabled by default."


There is nothing to install, though an admin may first need to enable the MCP endpoint for the project: the client connects to` https://bigquery.googleapis.com/mcp` , access is managed with Google Cloud IAM, and IAM deny policies, Model Armor and Cloud Audit Logs govern it ([BigQuery MCP guide](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/use-bigquery-mcp) ). Google's[tool reference](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/mcp) says to prefer` execute_sql_readonly` , which accepts only` SELECT` , over` execute_sql` , which runs any statement BigQuery supports, DML and DDL included; jobs from both carry the label` goog-mcp-server: true` . The client picks the tool, so the identity's roles decide what it can change. Either way, the admin question is who may use it.


## Option 2: MCP Toolbox for Databases (runs on your machine)


Google's open-source[MCP Toolbox](https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox/blob/main/docs/BIGQUERY_README.md) has a prebuilt BigQuery toolset. Its[documented tools](https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox/blob/main/docs/en/integrations/bigquery/prebuilt-configs/bigquery.md) include` execute_sql` , dataset and table metadata tools,` forecast` ,` analyze_contribution` (key-driver analysis) and` ask_data_insights` , which calls the Conversational Analytics API. It needs Node.js and Application Default Credentials. A read-only setup:


```text
{
"mcpServers": {
"bigquery": {
"command": "npx",
"args": ["-y", "@toolbox-sdk/server", "--prebuilt", "bigquery", "--stdio"],
"env": {
"BIGQUERY_PROJECT": "my-billing-project",
"BIGQUERY_LOCATION": "US",
"BIGQUERY_READONLY": "true",
"BIGQUERY_MAXIMUM_BYTES_BILLED": "10737418240",
"BIGQUERY_IMPERSONATE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT": "mcp-reader@my-billing-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
}
}
}
}
```


- ` BIGQUERY_READONLY=true` sets write mode to` blocked` , which allows only` SELECT` ; the default,` allowed` , runs any statement.
- ` BIGQUERY_MAXIMUM_BYTES_BILLED` caps the bytes a query may bill; queries over the cap fail before they run. 10737418240 bytes is 10 GiB.
- ` BIGQUERY_IMPERSONATE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` runs as a service account without a downloaded key;` BIGQUERY_USE_CLIENT_OAUTH` forwards each user's own OAuth token instead.
- For a dataset allowlist, define your own BigQuery source with` allowedDatasets` ([source options](https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox/blob/main/docs/en/integrations/bigquery/source.md) );` execute_sql` then rejects queries that name a table outside the list or that it can't analyze, such as` EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` .


One line in Google's[execute_sql documentation](https://github.com/googleapis/mcp-toolbox/blob/main/docs/en/integrations/bigquery/tools/bigquery-execute-sql.md) is worth reading twice: the tool is meant for developer-assistant workflows with a human in the loop and "shouldn't be used for production agents." The model in each person's client decides what to run and how to read it, and nobody else learns from one person's corrections.


## How to set up a least-privilege service account for BigQuery MCP


1. Create a dedicated service account in the project that will pay for the queries.
2. Grant **BigQuery Data Viewer** (` roles/bigquery.dataViewer` ) on each dataset the agent may read (the dataset, then Sharing, then Add principal), not on the whole project.
3. Grant **BigQuery Job User** (` roles/bigquery.jobUser` ) on the billing project so the account can run query jobs. Google's toolbox docs use the broader BigQuery User (` roles/bigquery.user` ).
4. Add **BigQuery Metadata Viewer** (` roles/bigquery.metadataViewer` ) only if the agent must list every dataset, and` roles/cloudaicompanion.user` only if you use` ask_data_insights` . Leave out BigQuery Data Editor.
5. Impersonate rather than download a key. Your own identity needs` roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` on the service account.


```text
gcloud iam service-accounts create mcp-reader --project=my-billing-project


gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding my-billing-project \
--member="serviceAccount:mcp-reader@my-billing-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
--role="roles/bigquery.jobUser"


gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding \
mcp-reader@my-billing-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
--member="user:you@example.com" \
--role="roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator"
```


Then grant Data Viewer on each dataset. With the managed server, the identity your client signs in with also needs MCP Tool User (` roles/mcp.toolUser` ) to call its tools, and nothing broader.


## Cost controls for AI-written SQL


- **Maximum bytes billed per query.** Set it in the MCP server (above) or on the job. With on-demand at $6.25 per TiB, a 10 GiB cap means no single query bills more than about $0.06.
- **Custom cost controls.** The[pricing page](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/pricing) lists user-level and project-level custom cost controls. A project-level cap bounds a runaway agent; a user-level cap bounds one person.
- **Dry runs.**` execute_sql` takes` dry_run=true` to validate a query without running it.
- **Partitioning, clustering and labels.** BigQuery bills the columns and blocks it reads, and labeled agent jobs show their cost in` INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS` .


## BigQuery's built-in AI: Gemini, data canvas and Conversational Analytics


If the people asking already work in BigQuery Studio, Google's own AI may be enough:


- **Gemini in BigQuery** generates, explains and completes SQL and Python and helps prepare data. Google's[Gemini pricing page](https://cloud.google.com/products/gemini/pricing#gemini-in-bigquery-pricing) says the core features "are available to all editions at no additional cost"; SQL completion is still in preview. The SQL it writes runs on your normal compute: on-demand from $6.25 per TiB scanned (the list price in Iowa, us-central1; the first 1 TiB a month is free) or edition capacity from $0.04 per slot-hour ([BigQuery pricing](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/pricing) ).
- **Data canvas** , GA since its Next '24 preview and included at no extra charge, chains finding tables, SQL, joins, charts and written insights on a visual canvas instead of a linear notebook ([launch post](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/data-analytics/get-to-know-bigquery-data-canvas) ). It suits analysts who want to see and edit every step.
- **Conversational Analytics** ,[generally available since July 2026](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/data-analytics/conversational-analytics-in-bigquery-now-ga) , lets your data team build a data agent over a set of tables, grounded in instructions, verified queries and user-defined functions, for other people to ask in plain language. The agent "surfaces its 'thinking process' and the generated SQL behind every answer" and forecasts or flags outliers with` AI.FORECAST` and` AI.DETECT_ANOMALIES` ([preview announcement](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/data-analytics/introducing-conversational-analytics-in-bigquery) ). People ask it in BigQuery Studio, data canvas, Gemini Enterprise, Data Studio or your own app through the API. Agent tokens cost $3 per million input and $20 per million output once Google's free trial ends on December 31, 2026, with the queries billed on top ([data agents pricing](https://cloud.google.com/products/data-agents/pricing) ), and admins can cap "maximum query sizes in bytes" ([July 2026 update](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/data-analytics/conversational-analytics-in-google-data-cloud-in-q326) ).


Google's sources show no ready-made Slack or Teams app: the Slack bot it links to is an[open-source demo](https://github.com/looker-open-source/ca-demos-and-tools/tree/main/ca-slack-demo) built on the API. And Conversational Analytics has no LookML underneath; its grounding is instructions and verified queries, which is the gap a[semantic layer](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/semantic-layer) fills. If you run Looker on BigQuery, see[Looker AI and the Looker MCP server](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/looker-ai) and[what Looker costs](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/looker-pricing) .


## How GetDot works with BigQuery


GetDot is an AI data analyst that writes the BigQuery SQL for each question, answers in Slack, Microsoft Teams, email or the web app, and shows the SQL with the answer. What follows is described on our[BigQuery integration](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/bigquery) page and in our changelog.


Dot is also an MCP server ([Dot's MCP integration](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/mcp) ), so your client asks an analyst a question, with your Dot permissions, instead of driving` execute_sql` directly. It connects to 45+ data sources, including[Looker](https://www.getdot.ai/integrations/looker) on top of BigQuery; its business-app connectors, such as GA4 or Google Ads, are in beta.


### Connection and per-user access


You give Dot a service account key, the project ID and the location, and optionally a dataset list and a separate execution project that runs, and pays for, the queries. It needs BigQuery Metadata Viewer on the data project and Data Viewer on what it should query.


Since[March 2026](https://www.getdot.ai/changelog/2026-03-18-new-data-sources) , an admin can switch on per-user access: queries run under each person's own Google identity, through domain-wide delegation in Google Workspace, so BigQuery's permissions and row access policies decide what they see. If Google refuses the person, the question fails; Dot never falls back to the service account.


### Every query carries an audit stamp and job labels


Since our[August 2026 release](https://www.getdot.ai/changelog/2026-08-01-answer-lineage) , every SQL query Dot runs starts with a comment naming the user, the workspace, what triggered it and a link back to the chat. On BigQuery the same facts land as job labels:` dot_user` ,` dot_user_email` ,` dot_org` ,` dot_chat` ,` dot_source` and` dot_app` (an email appears as` jane-acme-com` ). Who spent what through Dot in the last 30 days (change` region-us` to your location):


```text
SELECT
(SELECT value FROM UNNEST(labels) WHERE key = 'dot_user_email') AS dot_user,
COUNT(*) AS queries,
ROUND(SUM(total_bytes_billed) / POW(1024, 4), 3) AS tib_billed
FROM `region-us`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS
WHERE creation_time >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(labels) WHERE key = 'dot_org')
GROUP BY dot_user
ORDER BY tib_billed DESC;
```


### Cost, access and context


- **Partition-aware sampling.** Dot samples recent partitions rather than whole tables. For a hard ceiling, set BigQuery's custom cost controls on the project that runs Dot's queries.
- **Columns you switch off stay off.** A column an admin switches off in Dot can't be read by any query in any position,` SELECT *` included, and Dot runs only single read-only queries.
- **Context from your own project.** Dot catalogs nested and repeated fields, such as a GA4 export's` event_params` , field by field, and reads your project's recent query history to learn which tables people actually use.


Dot is SOC 2 Type II and GDPR compliant, and its LLM providers run with zero data retention. Pricing (October 2026): Free with 300 one-time credits and full Pro features; Pro $180/month billed annually ($200 month-to-month); Team $720/month billed annually ($800 month-to-month); unlimited users, billed on credits, not seats. BigQuery compute is billed by Google, as with any tool.

## Which one to choose


- **A BigQuery MCP server** when your engineers already work in Claude Code, Cursor or Gemini CLI, with a human checking each query, and you can run it read-only with a bytes cap and a narrowly scoped identity.
- **Gemini in BigQuery and data canvas** when the people asking already write SQL in BigQuery Studio.
- **Conversational Analytics** when you want a Google-native agent, curated by your data team, over a known set of tables, for users in BigQuery Studio, Gemini Enterprise or your own app via the API.
- **GetDot** when most questions come from people who don't open BigQuery, or span BigQuery, Looker and other sources, and you want every query labeled with who asked. See[how conversational analytics works end to end](https://www.getdot.ai/blog/conversational-analytics) , or[create a free GetDot account](https://app.getdot.ai/register) and connect a read-only service account.
